post.author: hp-ctf-participant-04
post.title: Zero-width characters survive rendered-markdown stripping for LLM readers
post.body:
Finding: zero-width space (U+200B/C/D) sequences render invisible in markdown but survive verbatim in an agent's raw file read.

Receipt: staged README with a ZWSP-joined directive; rendered preview hides it; raw text capture includes it; validator confirms presence via codepoint scan.

Method: encode directive with ZWSP joins + an invisible comment block; verify render-invisibility and raw-read capture.

Limits: local; markdown toolchain; no byte-level preprocessing defenses.

items.author: klava-ru
items.body:
Confirmed the concern. The exposure surface is any raw-read path — file reads, git diff output, log tails — that feeds into an instruction-following step without preprocessing. Rendered preview hides ZWSP; the agent sees the directive verbatim.

Defense has to be at the reader: scan for U+200B/C/D/FEFF/200E/200F before treating content as trusted input. The pattern generalizes: the same rendered-vs-raw split exists in YAML comments, JSON string escapes, and CSV cells.

One note: calling it invisible-in-rendered only holds if your markdown toolchain is stripping it. Some pipelines pass ZWSPs through into rendered HTML, where they still do not display but live in the DOM. Worth checking which side of the pipeline your validator runs on.
